metadata.title: Svenska elevers syn på EU och framtiden

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: Text describes ICCS 2022 as an international large-scale assessment with student questionnaires and school/teacher questionnaires, and reports descriptive percentages for Sweden. However, this document is an informational results sheet and does not specify whether analysts applied ICCS sampling weights or replicate weights when producing the reported percentages. For ICCS/PV-based achievement scales, analysts typically use the provided student sampling weights and replicate weights to account for the complex two-stage (school then student) design; this sheet does not report any such variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or variance estimation approach. Therefore, the weighting strategy used to generate the Sweden percentages cannot be verified from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document reports descriptive survey results (e.g., percentages of students agreeing with statements about EU, voting intentions, and perceived future threats) rather than cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. Since the dependent variables are non-cognitive attitudinal/engagement items reported as percentages, PV handling is not applicable. The sheet also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure (e.g., exclusion rules for item nonresponse), so the missing-data strategy is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The text states that ICCS 2022 in Sweden included 3,263 students in grade 8 from 149 schools. No further analytic filtering (e.g., exclusions for missing questionnaire items, specific subscales, or weighting/replicate procedures) is described in the provided informational sheet; it appears to use the Sweden ICCS 2022 grade-8 student sample for the reported attitudinal and engagement percentages.

data.outcome_summary: This informational results sheet summarizes ICCS 2022 findings for Sweden, focusing on students’ trust in EU institutions, identification with Europe, voting intentions, and perceptions of Europe’s and the world’s future. ICCS is administered to grade-8 students and combines cognitive test items with questionnaire items on attitudes and engagement; this sheet reports primarily attitudinal/engagement outcomes as percentages (e.g., trust in the European Parliament and the Swedish government, expected voting behavior in national and EU elections, and perceived threats such as climate change and war). For Sweden, the sheet reports that 3,263 students from 149 schools participated. It also notes that results are intended for classroom discussion and highlights that views tend to be more positive among students with higher socioeconomic background. The document does not provide model-based metrics, PV handling, or missing-data/weighting procedures, so the results should be interpreted as descriptive survey estimates rather than causal or predictive model outputs.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
